newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan's power outage cost estimated T$1 bln loss.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan's power outage cost estimated T$1 bln loss.

text.p: A 20-minute power outage in Taiwan's Hsinchu Science-based Industrial Park on Monday shut down operation of a great number of electronic firms, costing an estimated loss of over T$1 billion, officials said.

"The blackout took place in the afternoon, and many factories were unprepared, resulting in the damage of a large number of semi-finished products which were still in the manufacturing process," a spokesman of the park told Reuters.
He declined to estimate the amount of the loss, and said it would take about a week to work out the exact damage.
But some manufacturers gave the figure at around T$1 billion.

"On October 12 last year, there was a power outage for only 10 minutes, affecting one third of the factories in the zone, and it already cost T$400 million in damaged products," one manufacturer said.
United Micro and Taiwan Semi-Conductor Manufacturing were among some 300 firms being affected, park officials said.
The two companies, leading chip makers in Taiwan, were not immediately available for comment.
Taiwan Power Company said initial investigation showed the outage was caused by lightning which struck at a high-voltage cable in Hsinchu.
A total of 230,000 households in Hsinchu and neighbouring areas were affected, and power supply in some areas was only resumed an hour later, the power company said.
